name: Quality at a reasonable price
summary: Good returns on capital, a decent free-cash-flow yield, and margins in the top 25% of the sector.
how_to_read: Three filters must all pass: ROIC of at least 12%, a free-cash-flow yield of at least 4%, and an operating margin in the top 25% of the company’s own sector. The margin test is sector-relative, so a grocer is compared with grocers rather than with software companies. A sector with fewer than 5 companies that have an operating margin has no percentile, and its companies fail that test. Results are ranked by ROIC and FCF yield, half each. A reasonable price here means a reasonable FCF yield today, nothing more.
misses: Companies whose quality is temporarily hidden (heavy investment years, one-off charges).
Whether this year's cash flow will repeat: the screen can't tell.
